_new_items.feature: Composer placeholder rotation (new session vs follow-up)
_new_items.behavior: On an empty chat the composer placeholder cycles through 'What are we building?', 'Give Hermes a task', "What's on your mind?", 'Describe what you need', 'What should we tackle?', 'Ask anything', 'Start with a goal'; after the first turn it switches to 'Send follow-up' variants ('Send a follow-up', 'Add more context', 'Refine the request', "What's next?", 'Keep it going', 'Push it further', 'Adjust or continue'), and to 'Starting Hermes...' / 'Reconnecting to Hermes…' while the backend is not ready.

The queue panel lists parked turns with per-entry 'Edit', 'Delete', 'Send', 'Next' and 'Steer — redirect the live turn now' actions, an expand/collapse control ('Expand'/'Collapse') and a paused state ('{n} Queued — paused', 'Paused by Stop — resume sending the queued turns', 'Resume'); a lost turn reads 'Turn lost during restart' with 'Discard'/'Resume'.

The composer's context menu offers 'Prompt snippets…' ('Prompt snippets' — 'Pick a starter prompt to drop into the composer.'): 'Code review', 'Explain this' and 'Implementation plan', each dropping its text into the composer.
Right-clicking the composer offers a context menu (cut/copy/paste style actions plus composer-specific entries) rather than the browser default.

_new_items.feature: Completion drawer / command palette inside the composer
_new_items.behavior: A '/'-triggered completion drawer lists 'Commands', 'Skills' and 'Options' with a 'Browse all…' entry and a 'Hotkeys' help footer; each row shows an icon, the command, and its argument hint.

A voice menu ('Voice', 'Voice chat engine') lets the user pick the engine — 'GPT-Live (full-duplex, delegates to Hermes)' ('Needs an OpenAI API key') or 'speech-to-text' — with a fan of mute/unmute ('Mute microphone'/'Unmute microphone') and end controls.
With a wake word configured the composer shows its state: 'Wake word "{phrase}"', 'Wake word: "{phrase}" — listening', '— off' and '— paused during voice chat'.
While a turn runs, the send control reflects the busy-submit policy (submit-as-steer vs queue) instead of silently dropping the press.
A prompt that could not be delivered after a restart is offered back for discard or retry so the draft is not lost silently.
A message action 'Read aloud' speaks that reply ('Stop reading' while playing, 'Read aloud failed' on error, hint 'Shift-click: read the full response').
A per-message 'More actions' menu holds 'Copy', 'Copy full response', 'Branch in new chat', 'React', 'Read aloud', 'Restore checkpoint' ('Restore checkpoint — rerun from this prompt') and 'Review'.
Per-message checkpoint navigation: 'Restore previous checkpoint'/'Restore next checkpoint', opening a dialog 'Restore to this checkpoint?' with 'Restore & rerun'.
Scrolling to the top of a windowed transcript offers 'Show earlier messages'; loading the earlier window backfills without moving the viewport.
The transcript shows distinct wait copy: 'Hermes is loading a response', 'Processing prompt', and 'Loading {model} into memory' when a local model is being paged in.
Media references in replies render inline: images open on click, missing media falls back to 'Open {name}', and audio renders with a 'Preparing audio...' placeholder.

The tool feed shows a group header with counts and status ('N tool calls failed', 'Recovered after N failed steps', '1 step failed') and per-call status icons with accessible labels ('Running', 'Done', 'Error', 'Recovered').

Each tool row offers copy actions matched to its content: 'Copy command', 'Copy output', 'Copy code', 'Copy file', 'Copy path', 'Copy URL', 'Copy query', 'Copy results', 'Copy content', 'Copy activity' and 'Raw response'.

_new_items.feature: Tool timing and 'this turn took' footer
_new_items.behavior: A finished turn ends with 'This turn took {duration}' so per-turn cost is visible in the transcript.
'Always allow…' opens a dialog 'Always allow this command?' explaining the pattern that will be permitted ('Always allow' description) with confirm/cancel, so a permanent allow is reviewable.
When an approval is pending below the fold, a 'Approval needed' jump affordance appears (aria-label 'Approval needed') and scrolls the card into view.
A clarify with several questions shows '{answered} of {total} answered' and 'N questions' progress, staging one question at a time so later questions stay disabled behind an earlier one.
Right-clicking a session row opens the same action set as its menu ('Session actions'): Rename…, Pin/Unpin, Mark as read/unread, Archive, Export, Copy ID, New window, Open in new tab/split/terminal.
A '/session-import' route lets the user import sessions from another Hermes install (session.foreign.list/preview/import RPCs), with its own page rather than a chat.
'/command-center' hosts the command palette/center page opened by ⌘K/⌘P and ⌘. with 'Command palette' and a 'Close command center' control.
If the session store is damaged the sidebar shows 'Session database is damaged' with a recovery guide, the exact quit/inspect instruction and a 'Recovery guide' link instead of an empty list.

_new_items.feature: Sidebar header actions (new session in project, mark all read, search aria)
_new_items.behavior: The section header offers 'New session in {label}', 'Mark all as read' (disabled when nothing is unread) and hover-revealed actions; the search box is labelled 'Search sessions' for assistive tech.
A project has an 'Idea' field ('What's this project about? (saved to IDEA.md)') with 'Generate idea'/'Generating…' and 'Shuffle templates', persisted as IDEA.md in the project folder.

Kanban task worktrees (`<repo>/.worktrees/t_<hex>`, the t_… id kanban_db mints) never get their own sidebar lane — they collapse into one session-derived kanban bucket — while user-named 'New worktree' dirs (`<repo>/.worktrees/<slug>`) stay as their own lanes, so ephemeral task checkouts cannot blow the sidebar up into hundreds of empty rows.
Each worktree lane offers 'Remove worktree' ('Could not remove worktree (uncommitted changes?)'), 'Copy path' and 'Reveal in folder', and shows 'Worktrees' in the coding status bar.
